history.period: Original shrine c. 16th century; current structure early 20th century
history.summary: CSV DUPLICATE FLAG: this is the same temple as seq 861 'Karni Mata Temple' and seq 865 'Deshnoke Temple' (identical coordinates) - recommend merging the three CSV rows. CSV TOWN NORMALIZED: 'Deshnoke (Karni Mata)' reduced to 'Deshnoke' (also spelled Deshnok), Bikaner district, ~30 km south of Bikaner city. The world-famous 'Temple of Rats': some 20,000 black rats (kabas), believed to be reincarnated members of Karni Mata's family and devotees, are revered in the temple; spotting a rare white rat is considered highly auspicious, even a manifestation of the goddess herself. Legend: when Karni Mata's stepson Lakhan/Lakshman drowned (at Kapil Sarovar near Kolayat), she asked Yama to return him; when he could not, she decreed that no member of her clan would truly die but would be reincarnated as kabas - the Charan Kulhade legend. The inner shrine is centuries old; the present marble structure in late-Mughal/Rajput style with solid silver doors was built in the early 20th century by Maharaja Ganga Singh (reigned 1888-1943), and further marble carvings and silver gates were donated in 1999 by Kundanlal Verma of Karni Jewelers, Hyderabad. Legend also credits Karni Mata with laying the foundation stones of the Mehrangarh (Jodhpur) and Junagarh (Bikaner) forts. The twice-yearly fair draws thousands, many arriving on foot for the Oran Parikrama along a 42-km sacrosanct stretch. Date note: sources vary on Karni Mata's lifetime (14th vs 15th-16th century) - flagged.

name: Karni Mata Temple
town_description: Deshnoke (Deshnok) is a small temple town about 30 km south of Bikaner on the Bikaner-Jodhpur road, dominated by the Karni Mata Temple; some 600 Charan families here claim descent from Karni Mata and believe they will be reincarnated as the temple's kabas.

travel.railway: Bikaner Junction - about 30 km; Deshnoke has its own railway station closer to the temple (verify).
travel.road: On the Bikaner-Jodhpur road (NH62/NH89), ~30 km south of Bikaner; buses and taxis frequent; about 2 hours needed to see the whole temple.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; the fairs (March-April and September-October) for the full experience.
visitor_information.opening_hours: 4:00 AM - 10:00 PM; Mangla Aarti at 4:00 AM. No entry fee. Never harm or step on the kabas; sharing the rats' prasad and milk is considered auspicious (some believe the rats' saliva has healing properties). Offerings: 'dwar-bhent' to the priests, 'kalash-bhent' for temple upkeep.
